newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Agrobanka unit should join Slovak bank - NBS.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Agrobanka unit should join Slovak bank - NBS.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Thursday said the Slovak unit of the troubled Czech Agrobanka a.s should seek a Slovak bank, and not industrial companies, as a partner to start operating as an independent bank.
"The strategy of the NBS in this case is clear, meaning it (the partner of Agrobanka's Slovak unit) should be an existing Slovak bank," NBS spokesman Jan Onda told Reuters.
Agrobanka's Slovak unit said on Wednesday it was considering becoming a fully-independent bank from the beginning of 1997.
Under the plan, the Czech parent would hold 34 percent, and five unspecified large Slovak companies would share the remainder of the new bank's basic equity.
But Onda said the NBS would suggest for Agrobanka to join some already operating Slovak bank.
Onda added that the NBS still has not received any official request for approval of a new independent bank using Agrobanka's Slovak branches.

On Wednesday Vranislav Petroch, director of Agrobanka's Slovak unit, said those five companies, which he declined to name, would be lucrative Slovak companies from the chemical industry, of which only one has obligations to Agrobanka.

The announcement came a day after the Czech parent was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank because of poor liquidity stemming from the failure of another Czech bank, Kreditni Banka a.s.

Petroch said that Agrobanka Slovakia had three billion Slovak crowns in deposits and about 150 million crowns had been withdrawn since the Czech announcement on Tuesday. -- Tatiana Vacova, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
